extracted.intended_audience: Researchers (emerging and established) applying for SSHRC Insight Grants in the social sciences and humanities (Canada)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for preparing and submitting Insight Grant applications to SSHRC (October 2025 competition), including eligibility, funding streams, merit review criteria and scoring, and rules on use of grant funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Challenge — The aim and importance of the endeavour (40%)
rubrics_metrics.description: Originality, significance and expected contribution to knowledge; appropriateness of the literature review; appropriateness of the theoretical approach or framework; appropriateness of the methods/approach; quality of training and mentoring to be provided to students, emerging scholars and other highly qualified personnel, and opportunities for them to contribute; and potential for the project results to have influence and impact within and/or beyond the social sciences and humanities research community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weighted at 40% of the overall merit score. Committee members assign a numeric score (see scoring table) for this criterion; applications must receive a score of 3.0 or higher on each of the three main criteria to be recommended for funding. Includes evaluation of originality, methods, theoretical framing, literature, training/mentoring quality, and potential influence/impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility — The plan to achieve excellence (20%)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriateness of the proposed timeline, and probability that the objectives will be met; expertise of the applicant or team in relation to the proposed research; appropriateness of the requested budget, justification of proposed costs, and, where applicable, other cash and/or in-kind contributions; and quality and appropriateness of knowledge mobilization plans, including effective dissemination, exchange and engagement with stakeholders within and/or beyond the research community, where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weighted at 20% of the overall merit score. Assessors consider timeline realism, team expertise relative to the tasks, budget appropriateness and justification, and strength of knowledge mobilization/dissemination plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capability — The expertise to succeed (40%)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality, quantity and significance of past experience and published and/or creative outputs of the applicant and any co-applicants, relative to their roles in the project and to the stage of their career; evidence of past knowledge mobilization activities (e.g., films, performances, commissioned reports, knowledge syntheses, experience in collaboration / other interactions with stakeholders, contributions to public debate and media), and of impacts on professional practice, social services and policies, etc.; and quality and quantity of past contributions to the development, training and mentoring of students, postdoctoral researchers and other highly qualified personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weighted at 40% of the overall merit score. Committee members will consider only the last six years of research contributions (with accommodations for career interruptions). Evaluates track record and demonstrated capacity to carry out the proposed work and mentor/train others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring table and threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Numeric scoring descriptors and threshold for funding recommendation: 5–6 Very good to excellent; 4–4.9 Good to very good; 3–3.9 Satisfactory to good; Below 3 Unsatisfactory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Merit review committee members assign a score for each of the three criteria above using this table. The appropriate weighting is then applied to arrive at a final score. Applications must receive a score of 3.0 or higher for each of the three criteria to be recommended for funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject-matter eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals can involve any disciplines, thematic areas, approaches or subject areas eligible for SSHRC funding. Applications that would be more appropriately evaluated by NSERC or CIHR will not be accepted. Projects whose primary objective is curriculum development, program evaluation, preparation of teaching materials, organization of a conference or workshop, digitization of a collection, or creation of a database are not eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should consult SSHRC's subject matter eligibility guidelines. An application will be declared ineligible if 30% or more of the requested budget is allocated to ineligible expenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant eligibility (individuals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications can be submitted by an individual researcher or a team. Applicants (except postdoctoral fellows and PhD students) must be affiliated with a Canadian postsecondary institution that holds institutional eligibility at the time of application and before funding can be released. Researchers whose primary affiliation is non-Canadian are not eligible for applicant status. Applicants who have failed to submit required achievement reports are ineligible to apply until they do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Postdoctoral fellows are eligible to be applicants but must establish affiliation with an eligible Canadian postsecondary institution within five months of the grant start date for funds to be released. Enrolled students are not eligible unless they will have met all PhD requirements before the grant is awarded and establish affiliation within five months. Eligible PhD students and postdocs are advised to consult institutional research grants offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal scientists eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal scientists affiliated with a Canadian postsecondary institution must demonstrate that the proposed research or research-related activity is not related to the mandate of their employer or the normal duties for which they receive payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the proposal falls within the mandate of the federal government and the research is performed in government facilities, funding can only be allocated for student salaries, stipends and travel costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional eligibility and administration of funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Only eligible Canadian postsecondary institutions can administer grant funds awarded under this funding opportunity. Institutions proposing to administer a grant must hold or obtain institutional eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions seeking eligibility or with questions are encouraged to contact SSHRC’s Institutional Eligibility team at least 10 business days before the application deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-applicants and replacement rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals listed as co-applicants must meet the same eligibility criteria as applicants. Only a person who was named as a co-applicant in the original application can replace an applicant (principal investigator) for an Insight Grant-funded project, subject to program approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replacement of the applicant remains subject to program approval; co-applicant status in the original application is required to be eligible as a replacement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborators
rubrics_metrics.description: Any individual who makes a significant contribution to the project is eligible to be a collaborator. Collaborators do not need to be affiliated with an eligible Canadian postsecondary institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collaborators may be funded for travel/subsistence related to planning, exchange, and dissemination, but grant funds cannot be used for collaborators' research costs to conduct research or research-related activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple applications and holding multiple awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals can apply as an applicant for only one Insight Grant at a time. Normally, researchers cannot apply as an applicant for an Insight Grant and an Insight Development Grant within the same calendar year, with a specific exception allowing unsuccessful Insight Development Grant applicants from February to apply for Insight Grants in October of the same year. A researcher who applies for an Insight Grant in October 2025 can apply for an Insight Development Grant in February 2026 provided the objectives are significantly different.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See SSHRC’s regulations on multiple applications and holding multiple awards for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring, reporting and use of grant funds reporting obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Grant holders will be expected to report on the use of grant funds, on funded activities undertaken during the grant period, and on outcomes. Successful applicants will be informed of reporting requirements upon receiving their notice of award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be prepared to meet ongoing reporting obligations; specific reporting schedules/requirements will be provided with the notice of award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application process requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must complete the application form in accordance with the accompanying instructions. Applications must be submitted electronically by an authorized research grants officer, or equivalent, from the applicant’s institution. Eligible PhD students and postdoctoral fellows can submit their applications directly to SSHRC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants needing help preparing their application should communicate with SSHRC well in advance of the application deadline. Follow the Web CV, application and instructions provided by SSHRC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit review process (use of external assessors and committee deliberation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are reviewed through a competitive merit review process. Two groups are involved: external assessors and members of the Insight Grant merit review committees. SSHRC will seek, but cannot guarantee, a minimum of two external assessments per application. External assessors usually read only one application and provide their assessment; committee members read an entire cohort and the external assessments and evaluate and rank proposals. Merit review committees consider but are not bound by external assessors' judgments. Normally, applications initially determined by committee consensus to be ranked in the lowest 35% are not discussed during the final stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding decisions are based on committee recommendations and available funds; committee discussions are guided by the principle of minimum essential funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee structure and selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants will be asked in the application form to select the committee they consider most appropriate for review. Committee options include discipline-based; groups of disciplines; multi/interdisciplinary (one humanities-focused and one social sciences-focused, plus the Tri-Agency Interdisciplinary Peer Review Committee); and thematic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SSHRC will make efforts to accommodate applicant preferences but reserves the right to determine review process and committee assignment. For applications spanning more than one federal agency’s mandate, applicants can select the Tri-Agency Interdisciplinary Peer Review Committee which uses harmonized tri-agency review and specific evaluation criteria; the dominant component must be SSHRC-relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for Indigenous research merit review
rubrics_metrics.description: SSHRC’s Guidelines for the Merit Review of Indigenous Research are provided to help build understanding of Indigenous research and to assist committee members in interpreting SSHRC’s evaluation criteria in the context of Indigenous research. SSHRC relies on reviewers with Indigenous research experience to judge applicability. If enough Indigenous research applications are received, SSHRC can establish a distinct merit review committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These guidelines are relevant to applicants and reviewers; they can result in a more tailored merit review process for Indigenous research applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Future Challenge Areas are invited but not scored
rubrics_metrics.description: SSHRC invites applicants to consider addressing one or more of Imagining Canada’s Future’s 16 future global challenges in their proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is explicitly not an evaluation criterion for merit review and does not offer additional or dedicated research funds for this funding opportunity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value, duration and streams (funding envelope rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Insight Grants are valued at up to $500,000 over two to five years. A minimum request of $10,000 is required in at least one of the years. A maximum of $125,000 is available in a single year. Stream A: $10,000 to $125,000. Stream B: $125,001 to $500,000. Applicants choose stream based on amount requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both streams are adjudicated by the same committees and receive the same merit review; deadlines and application process are identical. The targeted success rate for Stream A is higher than for Stream B.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific rules for the use of grant funds (eligible/ineligible expenditures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Grant funds cannot be used to remunerate team members regardless of eligibility (including postdoctoral fellows serving as team members), except in some cases Indigenous team members may be compensated per Tri-agency guideline; grant funds cannot be used for remuneration and/or travel and subsistence costs of presenters or guest speakers; cannot be used for course release time; can be used for consulting fees for expert/professional/technical services that contribute directly to proposed research if not provided by a team member; can be used for travel/subsistence costs of collaborators related to research planning, exchange and dissemination but not for collaborators' research costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Indigenous team members are compensated under the exception, they may not be delegated to authorize grant expenditures and the applicant/project director cannot be compensated from grant funds. Applicants are advised to consult the Tri-agency Guide on Financial Administration and the Use of Grant Funds section for permissible expenditures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulations, policies and related compliance (including STRAC and tri-agency policies)
rubrics_metrics.description: All applicants and grant holders must comply with the Regulations Governing Grant Applications and the Tri-agency Guide on Financial Administration. Grant holders must comply with the Tri-Agency Open Access Policy on Publications and the Tri-Agency Research Data Management Policy. The Policy on Sensitive Technology Research and Affiliations of Concern (STRAC) applies and may disqualify proposals involving sensitive technology research where researchers have problematic affiliations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should consult tri-agency guidance on STRAC to understand impacts. SSHRC reserves the right to determine eligibility and to interpret regulations and policies governing its funding opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication of results and feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: SSHRC makes competition results available to applicants and institutions. All applicants will be provided, in addition to SSHRC’s notice of decision, any external assessments received, and a summary of the merit review committee’s evaluation of their proposal, where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment reports and committee summaries are provided via the SSHRC Extranet for Applicants and the Grants and Scholarships Administration Portal for institutions.
